A1.justification: Both PDFs describe STORM, with clearly corresponding SOM, HSFA, TOM, and benchmark experiments despite substantial revisions. All pages, including appendices A–F in v1 and A–H in v3, are available and readable; text extraction and visual inspection support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation, pose estimation, tracking recovery, and failure-classification results in Tables 1–4, plus ablations in Appendix E.

after.justification: v3 reports original benchmark results and additional reconstruction, reference-count, runtime, and temporal-robustness experiments in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: v3 adds SAM3D reconstruction from reference images, replaces DINOv2 with DINOv3, and revises HSFA conditioning and the active segmentation losses. TOM retains BCE-based verification but adds EMA smoothing, three-frame persistence, and controlled FIFO memory updates. These change the input pipeline, learned components, and recovery procedure beyond renaming or implementation disclosure.

E1.justification: The five BOP segmentation benchmarks and LM-O/YCB-Video pose benchmarks remain. However, v3 adds SA-V to SOM training, no longer lists TYOL in the training mix, and evaluates reference-image reconstruction and pose estimation using reconstructed geometry. This substantially extends the training and input-scenario coverage beyond v1's supplied-model pipeline.

E2.justification: CosyPose is added to the supervised segmentation comparison in Table 2. New diagnostic experiments also compare temporal recovery against per-frame binary triggering and aligned reconstruction against unaligned/ground-truth geometry. The principal CNOS, FoundationPose, cosine-similarity, and TOM attention comparison sets otherwise remain.

E3.justification: The main segmentation comparison changes from the 16-rendered-view setup to one reference with language conditioning, with variable reference sampling during training. Appendix D revises the SOM optimization recipe, including learning rates and gradient clipping. v3 also explicitly reports pose scores as AUC, adds AUROC, and introduces controlled geometry and temporal-noise protocols. These reported changes do not establish that every retained experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds reconstruction/alignment controls, reference-count-by-language ablations, component runtime profiling, and transient-noise tests of temporal recovery. Language, HSFA-depth, and backbone fine-tuning analyses already existed in v1. The HSFA-depth values and original ablation graphics are retained; notably, the fine-tuning graphic is relabeled from DINOv2 to DINOv3 without establishing a new run.

E5.justification: v1 provides limited timing spreads without corresponding run-count documentation. v3 introduces five-run/seed means and standard deviations for pose, segmentation, reconstruction, and verifier comparisons, plus ten-repeat runtime profiling. Baseline uncertainty remains largely unavailable. This is a substantial reporting expansion, not evidence that v1 necessarily used fewer runs.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces SOM's 68.5 mean AP with 67.7 under the revised single-reference configuration, so this is not a same-setting performance decline. Table 1 changes YCB-Video AR from 0.74 to 73%, while tracking and classifier accuracy means are retained. Reconstruction, AUROC, reference-count, runtime, and temporal-noise results substantially expand the reported evidence.

T1.justification: v3 revises the mathematical normalization and loss definitions and adds a similarity-transform alignment objective and formal temporal detection/calibration rules in Appendices G–H. These are limited mathematical extensions without new theorems or proofs. Negating the existing verifier logit and restating standard metric formulas do not independently constitute substantial theoretical advances.

C1.justification: The central input claim changes from requiring a supplied 3D model to operating from a reference image without curated CAD at deployment. v3 replaces broad self-supervised/label-free claims with annotation-free, adaptation-free inference after offline training, and emphasizes variable-reference fusion and persistent drift verification. This substantially redefines the contribution's scope.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly limits zero-shot claims because object identities can overlap between training and testing. It also distinguishes CAD-assisted benchmark alignment from deployment, qualifies reconstruction fidelity, separates initialization costs from steady-state tracking, and discusses language quality, threshold calibration, and difficult object materials/shapes. These substantive applicability boundaries were largely absent from v1.

D1.justification: v3 adds the exact semantic prompt and postprocessing, descriptor caching, detailed optimizer groups and precision/batch settings, runtime software and hardware, ICP sampling, and TOM calibration/memory parameters. Appendix H also specifies probabilities and mask geometry for the already-existing YCB-Video stress test. The code-access pointer changes; external availability was not checked.

R1.justification: Related work is reorganized around reference-conditioned segmentation, geometric priors, and tracking verification. New discussions include SAM3, DINOv3, SAM3D, Pos3R, Direct3D-S2, reconstruction methods, and energy-based scoring. HSFA is positioned more explicitly as a task-specific composition of established attention operations, substantially revising the novelty context.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, method, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Experimental questions are reorganized from four to five, subsections become more structured, and dedicated limitations and expanded technical appendices reshape the narrative. The title, author information, and publication formatting also change.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn for image references and SAM3D, and a reconstruction-comparison figure is added. Tables gain uncertainty displays, AUROC, revised supervision groupings, and new reconstruction, runtime, reference-count, and temporal-noise displays. The conference layout changes throughout, while several original qualitative and ablation figures are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially improves scientific assessability by replacing v1's contradictory label-free training framing with explicit supervised offline training and narrower inference claims, adding uncertainty reporting and diagnostic controls, and documenting reproduction-critical procedures. These address important weaknesses in v1. Limitations remain: strong reconstructed-geometry results depend on CAD alignment for benchmarking, the DINO ablation graphic is reused under a changed backbone label, and Section 4.1 still claims exact oracle matching despite lower YCB-Video values in Table 1. The substantial gains in transparency and experimental support outweigh these unresolved issues.
